newsitem.title: USA: Compaq extends PC sales lead, Dell rises-IDC.
newsitem.headline: Compaq extends PC sales lead, Dell rises-IDC.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp's widened it lead in both the U.S. and worldwide personal computer market in the first quarter, while Dell Computer Corp scored a 39 percent rise in market share, according to an industry report.

International Data Corp said Compaq's market share rose to 11.1 percent, up from 10 percent a year ago. Compaq, which shipped 2.02 million units in the period, has been the market leader for six quarters in a row, IDC said.
International Business Machines Corp was second with a global share of 8.8 percent, on shipment of 1.6 million units, IDC said.
Dell, boosted by a 60 percent rise in unit shipments, grabbed a 5.3 percent share, up from 3.8 percent one year ago. The mail order-only PC maker shipped 970,000 units.

Dell squeezed past IBM into third place on the list of U.S. PC makers, with an 8.2 percent market share. Dell's desktop sales were especially healthy and the overall total was boosted by growth in notebooks and Dell's increasing presence in the server market, IDC said.

"Dell's ascent was propelled by increasing acceptance of its OptiPlex desktops among major corporations," said John Brown of IDC. "It is also becoming more of a true global force, with strong sales in Europe and a rising presence in Japan."

Closely held Packard Bell NEC Inc was the fourth on the global list and second in the U.S. market, on shipments of 905,000 units. IDC said Packard Bell's new $799 PC has become its best selling model.

Toshiba Corp rose to fifth on the worldwide scale, on the strength of its dominant position in the portables market. The firm shipped 891,000 units in the first quarter, a 60 percent jump over the 558,000 shipped a year ago, IDC said. IDC said a total of 18.2 million units were shipped globally in the first quarter, up 16 percent from 1996.
